Question: What is wrong with making Hindi as our national language?
Answer: As per indian constitution, India has 22 official languages. 1) Assamese, (2) Bengali, (3) Gujarati, (4) Hindi, (5) Kannada, (6) Kashmiri, (7) Konkani, (8) Malayalam, (9) Manipuri, (10) Marathi, (11) Nepali, (12) Oriya, (13) Punjabi, (14) Sanskrit, (15) Sindhi, (16) Tamil, (17) Telugu, (18) Urdu (19) Bodo, (20) Santhali, (21) Maithili and (22) Dogri. Article 351 separates the Hindi language from all official languages of India and makes it a special language of India. Now the promotion of Hindi is not limited to the boundary of India. India hosted the G20 Summit in New Delhi last year in which several world leaders participated including US President Joe Biden. PM Modi addressed the opening ceremony in Hindi. Question: Is the Bengaluru water crisis as severe as it is portrayed by the media, or is it exaggerated as usual?
Answer: I have been in Bangalore for more than 10 years. I think the media is not even portraying properly the severity of the water crisis that Bangalore is going through currently. Bangalore primarily gets its water supply from two sources - the Cauvery river and groundwater. For most non-drinking uses, recycled water processed by sewage treatment plants is used. With no rain for a while now, the primary sources have been stretched to their limits. Bengaluru needs 2,600-2,800 million litres of water daily, and the current supply is half of what's required. The result is a daily struggle for the city's residents. Leave about individual struggle now the situation is like even a few hospitals are facing a water crisis problem they are completely dependent on the water tanker supply and for your information a water tanker which usually cost earlier Rs 500–700 now costing Rs 1800–2000 now think who will pay this extra bill?. IT engineers crying to work from home now not for their comfort or to save high rent because Work-from-home will be a viable option, but only if people actually go home so that the population is reduced and water consumption drops. Now after seeing this situation government to restricting and capping private tankers for price they are refusing to supply water at many residential places just think what was will be the situation in that place? The government put fines over using of drinking water in swimming pools, car washing etc. It affected several swimming sports clubs in Bangalore. A city which is famous for its weather and the weather is so unpredictable that people are always advised to carry an umbrella because you never know when the rain will start happening but now from months we are just looking in the clear sky hoping for the Rain.
